Remember this: self-service machines can handle 80% of routine ticketing, but the remaining 20% of unexpected and difficult situations, including schedule disruptions, overbooking, complex rebooking, and traveler emotions, are why counters still exist.

This work does not suit people who are impatient, quick-tempered, or reluctant to speak. If travelers ask the same question one hundred times, you must answer it one hundred times. Complaints and shouting are also part of the job.

A common path is: an associate degree or a major related to tourism management or aviation services → employment at an airport, station, travel agency, or ticketing platform → proficiency in ticketing systems and change and refund rules → occupational skills certification such as civil aviation passenger service agent → advancement to shift supervisor, service manager, or operations management.

This work suits people who communicate clearly, work quickly, and can remain seated for extended periods. During peak periods, dozens of people can be waiting, so you must process transactions quickly and accurately while absorbing travelers' negative emotions.

Reservation and Transportation Ticket Agents and Travel Clerks provide travelers with booking, ticket issuance, changes, refunds, itinerary searches, and inquiry services. They handle special needs and disruptions to keep transportation services operating smoothly.

entries: Reservation and transportation ticket agents and travel clerks provide travelers with booking, ticket issuance, changes, refunds, itinerary searches, and inquiry services. They handle special needs and exceptional situations to keep transportation services operating smoothly.
Process bookings, ticket issuance, changes, and refunds.
Search schedules and provide itinerary advice to travelers.
Handle disruptions such as flight delays, cancellations, and overbooking.
Assist travelers with special needs, including older adults, children, and wheelchair users, with required procedures.
Verify identity and ticket information and process fare settlements.
Answer inquiries, handle complaints, and maintain service records.

paragraphs: Counter work can feel like a battle. During peak season, lines extend beyond the barriers as you issue tickets at the keyboard while listening for the next traveler's question. Phone calls and online service tickets keep arriving too. Schedule disruptions are the most chaotic: dozens of people gather to ask about rebooking, and you must check the system while prioritizing cases. Even when your voice grows hoarse, you must remain courteous.

In short: book and issue tickets, process changes and refunds, search schedules, handle disruptions, and assist travelers with special needs. Specific duties include ticket processing, itinerary searches, disruption handling, assistance for travelers with special needs, fare settlement, and inquiry and complaint handling.
Handling schedule disruptions and exceptional situations

BLS projects 3% employment growth from 2024–2034 (BLS OOH, 2026). Online and self-service adoption is a clear trend, and conventional ticket-counter roles will continue to contract. However, growth in travel volume and complex itineraries will sustain demand for advanced ticketing professionals skilled in schedule disruption handling, connecting itineraries, and services for travelers with special needs.

AI can find the optimal schedule and issue a ticket in one second, but when a flight is canceled, dozens of stranded travelers need more than a link. They need someone who can make decisions.

Data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) show that about 131,900 reservation and transportation ticket agents and travel clerks were employed in 2024. Employment is projected to rise to 135,600 by 2034, a net increase of about 3,700 jobs, with approximately 14,400 openings each year. The median annual wage was about $41,500 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not eliminate the entire occupation, but it will absorb a large share of routine operations. Online check-in, self-service ticketing, and AI customer service have already replaced most basic fare searches, ticket issuance, and simple changes and refunds. The remaining value lies in disruption handling, connecting-itinerary coordination, services for travelers with special needs, and emotional reassurance. The more automated the system becomes, the more valuable these fallback responsibilities become.

paragraphs: A score of 5/10 indicates an occupation with a moderately high degree of standardization. AI and self-service equipment have taken over many routine ticketing operations, but counter staff remain indispensable for exception handling and interpersonal service.

Moderately high exposure means that ticket agents who only know how to operate systems are declining in number, while service professionals who can handle complex situations are becoming more valuable. Spend less effort memorizing procedures and more time practicing disruption handling and communication. Once AI completes the easy work, the difficult cases define your role.

For those seeking careers in airline or rail service, education and academic specialization are only entry credentials; service awareness and adaptability are the core capabilities. Participate in social activities during college to practice communication. Do not expect to remain at a service window for an entire career; plan to advance into management or operations.

Make schedule-disruption handling, connecting-itinerary coordination, and services for travelers with special needs your signature capabilities. Proactively learn new ticketing systems and big-data processing tools, then advance toward roles such as shift supervisor, service quality specialist, or operations manager.

People with customer service, sales, or administrative backgrounds generally transition smoothly. Highlight experience handling complaints and high-volume demand on your resume. Enter the field first, then earn credentials such as the civil aviation passenger service agent certification and work toward management.

As self-service expands, counter-service hiring should focus on service-oriented talent who can handle exceptions and reassure travelers. Reposition the role as a travel concierge or service specialist, and provide advancement paths for highly capable employees.

This work suits people who enjoy bringing order to chaos. The more disorderly a disruption becomes, the more clearly your value shows. When travelers leave the counter grateful that their problems were solved, you feel that although the job is noisy, you genuinely helped someone.

The most heartwarming part of this work is helping people solve urgent problems. When a flight is delayed, you help an older traveler rebook onto the earliest departure and coordinate the connection. They clutch the new ticket and thank you repeatedly. You solved what the system could not.
Conventional C + Enterprising E + Social S

If you can withstand the noise of peak periods, patiently answer repeated questions, and still want to help people straighten out their journeys amid chaos, this service career offers steady rewards and a path upward.

Online check-in, self-service ticket machines, and AI customer service are replacing many routine ticketing operations, and counter roles continue to contract. People who only follow system prompts face high risk, while those who can handle complex rebooking, reassure travelers, and coordinate connecting itineraries are becoming scarcer.

AI can issue a ticket in three seconds, but an older traveler stranded after a flight cancellation needs more than an automated rebooking confirmation. They need to hear, 'Don't worry, I'll help you make arrangements.' That human warmth is the irreplaceable foundation of this service occupation.

subject.name: Reservation And Transportation Ticket Agents And Travel Clerks
subject.summary: Reservation and transportation ticket agents and travel clerks are the people who help every journey depart smoothly. Changes, refunds, and connecting-itinerary coordination seem routine, but if mishandled, they can ruin an entire trip.
